group.label: Derivatives
group.comment: Applies to images asked for by path through the Media ViewModel — CMS and wysiwyg art. Catalog images keep going through Magento's own image pipeline and are not touched.

field.label: Enabled
field.comment: Off: templates still get intrinsic width and height (so layout stays stable), but the payload carries only the original URL. Existing derivatives are left on disk, so switching back on is instant.

field.label: Width ladder (CSV px)
field.comment: Sorted and de-duplicated on read; values outside 16-8192 are dropped. Rungs wider than about 90% of the source are dropped per image, so a small upload simply gets fewer rungs rather than an upscale.

field.label: Encoder quality
field.comment: 1-100, clamped. Applies to the source-format ladder. A derivative that lands heavier than the original is discarded in favour of the original bytes, so raising this wastes CPU long before it wastes bandwidth.

group.label: WebP
group.comment: A second, parallel srcset. It is emitted only when every rung encoded successfully and came out smaller than the source — a partial WebP set would let a browser pick an under-resolution rung for a full-width slot.

field.label: Enabled
field.comment: Requires GD built with WebP support. Without it the payload silently carries the source-format ladder only.

group.label: Limits
group.comment: Derivatives are produced during the render that first needs them. These two fields are what keeps that from turning into an unbounded request.

field.label: Maximum source megapixels
field.comment: GD decodes to roughly 4 bytes per pixel before any resize happens, so this is a memory ceiling expressed in the only unit the header probe can read without decoding. Sources above it are served as-is.

field.label: Maximum encodes per request
field.comment: Shared by every image on the page. Rungs are generated widest-first, so when the budget runs out the srcset that render is short of its small rungs, never its large ones. The next render continues where this one stopped.
